newsitem.title: USA: Slew of new corp junk bond deals to hit U.S market.
newsitem.headline: Slew of new corp junk bond deals to hit U.S market.

text.p: Over $500 million in new high-yield junk bonds are expected to be sold in the U.S. market by the end of the week, syndicate officials said.
As of Thursday, Wall Street officials believed buyside demand for the new securities will be more than enough to absorb the new supply.
"The market is extremely strong becuase of the tremendous amount of new cash that has poured into high-yield mutual funds," said one syndicate official.
"Investor preference for risk is also extrememly high as a result of the need to put new cash to work," he added.
High-yield offerings expected to price on Thursday and Friday are:

-CFP Holdings's $110 million offering of 144a senior guaranteed notes due 2004 via NationsBanc Capital Markets. Price talk on the deal, expected to come to market on Thursday morning, is around 11.75 percent, market players said.

-Petro Stopping Centers' $125 million offering of 144a senior notes due 2007 via CIBC Woody Gundy Securities Corp. Price talk on the deal, expected to price on Thursday, is around 10.75 percent, according to market sources.

-Perez Companc SA's offering of $200 million in 144a notes due 2004 via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc. Sources say price talk on the deal, expected to hit the market on Thursday, is 250-275 basis points. Perez is an Argentine oil and gas company.
-Derlan Manufacturing Inc's offering of $100 million in 144a senior unsecured notes due 2007 via BT Securities Inc. Sources say price talk is 10 percent to 10.25 percent.
Sources say American Radio Systems Corp plans to sell $150 million in cumulative exchangeable PIK preferred securities via Credit Suisse First Boston on Friday.
In the high-grade new issue market, a unit of Texas Utilities Co plans to sell $500 million in trust preferred securities on Thursday via Goldman Sachs & Co.
The deal will include floating-rate and a fixed-rate tranches. The size of each tranch has yet to be determined, according to a company official.

Market sources say Xerox Corp plans to sell $500 million in fixed-rate, 30-year trust preferred securities in a 144a offering via Merrill Lynch & Co on Thursday. The securities will not be callable for 10-years, they add.
Manufacturer's Life Financial is also rumored to be be preparing a $500 million trust preferred deal, according to market sources.
